The board said the investigation will consider all available information, though it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised." For years he has ridden two horses at once: the foreign-policy restrainers, who want to reduce America’s overseas military commitments, and more traditional Republicans, who regard military power and robust alliances as essential to maintaining America’s international position. Trump has borrowed from both. Like the restrainers, he wants to avoid open-ended wars and military occupations. Like the traditional Republicans, he wants to prevent hostile powers from dominating strategically important regions. His preferred solution is to preserve American influence through economic coercion, selective military force, and capable regional allies.
